entities.speaker: Jessica Dalton
entities.comment-context: Written public comment read into the record

segments.text: June 16, 2020 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:

Mayor Frost,

I am a born and raised citizen of American Fork as is my husband. We both love this city so much that we knew it was the place we wanted to raise our children and so when it came time to buy, we were thrilled to find a place in what we have always considered our home town.

I have always had a good experience with our police force, but my experience is as a white member of our city with privilege. I believe that we can always do more to make American Fork better, especially as our city grows and the demographic of our city changes.

While I was pleased to read the response from Chief Darren Falslev, it felt more like a “these are all the great things we are doing” rather than a letter explaining the things they are doing but how they will improve upon them.

First the mention of “all lives matter”, while I believe the sentiment to be sincere by Chief Falslev, this is a phrase that is used to dismiss and silence the struggles and prejudices that our black brothers and sisters as well as other marginalized groups go through. I want to see this phrase, as well as other phrases that are used to dismiss and undermine the excess force against black people, removed from public documents. Some other phrases include “color blind” and “blue lives matter”.

I am glad to see that all officers receive CIT training, however, it’s concerning that not all of them receive the training from the Arbinger Institute Outward Mindset curriculum. Why is it that we are not training all of our officers with this curriculum especially when it is states that the department values each individual? I would like to see this as an improvement by our police force to have each officer receive this training.

Another thing that can be vastly improved upon is to have the body cams worn always, not just regularly. This not only protects our police force but our community and residents as well.

And along with that, when investigations are needed, we need to have them done by an independent civilian review board and not by an internal investigation board. This board would be democratically elected, not appointed by local Mayors or Governors as well as it must not include current police officers or relatives of police officers. By voting for the members of these boards, it with accountability and transparency which we need to protect the people.

I believe that the by doing these things, we can make American Fork better and a more welcome place as it continues to grow. I want to continue to say that American Fork is a great place to live as we move into the future.

Jessica Dalton

entities.speaker: Claudia Rasmussen
entities.comment-context: Written public comment read into the record

segments.text: June 16, 2020 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:

Hello city council,

Here is what I expect from the American Fork Police Department.

No use of phrases in public documents that have been used to undermine the excess use of force by police against black people. Some of these are All Lives Matter, Color Blind, and Thin Blue Lines Matter.

Every officer not just those with the "Advanced Officer status" should be trained in the Arbinger Institute Outward Mindset that emphasizes the intrinsic value of every individual.

Our police department needs to be investigated by democratically elected, independent civilian review boards; which have the power to investigate police, and also bring charges against police.

These boards must have subpoena power. These boards must not include current police officers or relatives of police officers. The people on these boards must not be appointed by local Mayors, or Governors. We want the ability to vote for the members of these boards and have them give us the accountability and transparency which is needed to protect the people.

Body-worn cameras need to be worn not on a regular basis but AT ALL TIMES.

We need these changes now!

entities.speaker: Lex Scott
entities.comment-context: Written public comment read into the record

segments.text: June 16, 2020 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Lex Scott, Founder of Black Lives Matter Utah

A democracy allows for live comments. I suggest that in the future you allow the public comment. It is imperative that your staff attend implicit bias training. It is important that we know how you plan to address and deal with racism in policing. It is imperative that we know your stance on police reform. This should happen soon so that we know who to re-elect and who to canvass against. Thank you
